<thought>After several attempts to locate a specific carbonyl‑ene template in the catalog, I concluded that the most reliable single‑step retrosynthetic disconnection is the reverse of the intramolecular carbonyl‑ene reaction. In the forward direction the reaction forms a C–O bond (producing the secondary alcohol) and a C–C bond that creates the five‑membered ring, while breaking a C=O (ketone) and a C=C (alkene). Reversing this gives two simple precursors that are commercially available: (1) styrene, which provides the exocyclic alkene attached to the phenyl ring, and (2) 1‑(trifluoromethyl)cyclopentan‑1‑one, which provides the ketone and the CF₃‑substituted carbon. Connecting these two fragments via a carbonyl‑ene cyclisation furnishes the target molecule in one step. The retrosynthetic route is therefore represented as a single reaction node linking the target to these two precursors.</thought>
